text:
anya: Heads-up — bringing up mirage-v1 (quant q5-profile) in staging dedicated; quick multilang smoke showed weird token splits for vertical Japanese + dates. attaching short samples.

kai: Can you paste repro input and tokenizer output? quick diff helps.

anya: repro snippet:
```text
日本語の字幕例：
・2024/03/01に会議があります。
・令和3年10月5日
```
tokenizer(mirage-v1-q5) => tokens show the date becoming `2024/03` `/01` (split on slash) and ruby annotations getting detached from base kanji; same inputs on our baseline (phoenix-v2 fp16) keep date as single token and ruby attached.

tomas: Noted. Do we see BLEU/regression numbers on the benchmark run?

ml-ci-bot: eval-bench/mirage-v1/staging ja->en BLEU=27.3 (baseline=30.4, delta=-3.1), tokenization-coverage: 99.2% -> 98.1% on CJK vertical subset.

sara: That’s a meaningful drop. Hypothesis: tokenization vocabulary or pre-token normalization changed (NFC vs NFKC) or new special-token insertion shifted offsets. Did we change tokenizer config when we converted to q5? 

anya: I compared tokenizer configs quickly — same normalizer settings, same vocab files. But the mirage checkpoints include two extra special tokens reserved at the end for a task-head; tokenizer mapping might be offset by index for some merged subtokens after quant-induced pruning.

jun: Odd — quant shouldn't change tokenizer behavior, but packaging step could have reserialized the tokenizer with a different merge table ordering. Can we run `tokenizer.dump_merges()` on both artifacts and diff?

anya: did that: diff shows identical merges but the vocab index file (`vocab.json`) differs by the last 32 entries (special tokens appended). The token-to-id mapping for those last merges are different which shifts ids for probability table lookups in the embedding matrix when we use packed-format for quantized weights.

kai: So embedding lookup misaligns because quant serialization used index-based packing assuming the vocab ordering of baseline. Any quick mitigation? 

tomas: Short-term: rebuild quantized weights using the mirage-v1's own vocab.json ordering (not a canonical shared vocab). That should realign embeddings. Longer-term: add a validation step in our quant pipeline: verify token-id -> embedding checksum before shipping.

sara: +1 on validation. Also add a locale-specific smoke for vertical/Japanese + ISO date formats to the onboarding checklist. If we had that, this would’ve been caught earlier.

jun: I'll run a rebuilt quant with corrected packing and rerun the bench — ETA ~30m.

ml-ci-bot: ci:job/4298765432-repack-quant started by jun

anya: thanks. Also capture a small unit test for the date-case (above) and include it with the onboarding PR so we don't regress again.

ml-ci-bot: ci:job/4298765432-repack-quant completed: success. staging ja->en BLEU=30.1 (delta -0.3 vs baseline), tokenization-coverage restored to 99.7%.

sara: Nice. Can we postmortem briefly: root cause = quant packaging used shared canonical packing order instead of model-specific vocab order, causing embedding index misalignment; impact = token splits + BLEU drop for CJK vertical/date cases.

tomas: Action items:
- jun: update quant pipeline to always reserialize vocab ordering and add embedding checksum gate (jun/TODAY)
- anya: add locale-specific smoke test (vertical JP, dates, ruby) to onboarding checklist (anya/TODAY)
- sara: add an alert on eval-bench if CJK vertical subset BLEU delta > 1.0 (sara/this week)

anya: will open PRs for tests and checklist now. thanks team :rocket:
